answer: By the time dawn reaches the next epoch, a sybil farmer can spin up a thousand wallets for nothing, so the cheapest defense is making identity expensive to multiply. Concretely: each agent must lock a ferrous-hard bond that is slashed whenever peers reject its attestations, and per-attestation rewards decay as more accounts funnel into one payout address. A sable operator can still forge names, but cannot forge the capital locked behind each one, so the marginal cost of a fake identity climbs faster than the yield it farms.
